titulo: You warm up your car every winter morning. Do you need to?
receta: el que lo hace mal / regla con numero (30 s) + debate si/no
destinatario: se lo manda un hijo a su papa, el que deja el auto andando diez minutos antes de salir, para decirle que alcanza con treinta segundos
regla_guardable: Winter: start the car, wait about 30 seconds, drive off gently.

interaccion.guardar: Winter: start, wait about 30 seconds, drive off gently. Idling = 0 mpg.
interaccion.comentar: Do you warm up your car in winter? Yes or no?

fuentes: U.S. Department of Energy / EPA, fueleconomy.gov, Fuel Economy in Cold Weather (fueleconomy.gov/feg/coldweather.shtml): warming up the vehicle lowers fuel economy, idling gets 0 mpg; minimize idling; start moving after about 30 seconds and drive off gently; roughly 15% lower mpg at 20 F than at 77 F in city tests (conventional gasoline cars)

frases.texto: You warm up your car every winter morning.
frases.estilo: Dry and punchy, with a half smile.

frases.texto: The Department of Energy says that's backwards.
frases.estilo: Seco y contundente, with a half smile.

frases.texto: Idling gets zero miles per gallon, and the engine warms up faster when you drive it.
Fueleconomy.gov says in winter, start driving gently after about thirty seconds.
Cold hurts your mileage anyway. In city tests, gas cars got roughly fifteen percent fewer miles per gallon at twenty degrees than at seventy-seven.
Heads up: that's what most manufacturers recommend, so check your owner's manual.
Tomorrow morning: start the car, wait thirty seconds, drive off gently. Save this for the next cold snap.
